把混亂整理成結構的人。面對模糊的任務，你會先建立框架、流程與優先順序，讓事情變得: The one who turns chaos into structure. Faced with a vague task, you first build the framework, the process and the priorities, so the work becomes doable.
無法忍受長期的混亂，看到沒有秩序的東西會自動想「這要怎麼落地」。: You can't stand ongoing chaos. When something has no order, you automatically think, "how do we make this real?"
擅長分類、排序、定規則——別人卡住的時候，你畫得出流程圖。: You're good at sorting, ordering and setting rules. When others are stuck, you can draw the flowchart.
接到新任務的第一反應是拆解：目標是什麼、步驟有哪些、誰負責哪段。: Your first reaction to a new task is to break it down: what's the goal, what are the steps, who owns which part.
壓力大的時候，會想把所有變數都抓在手上。: Under pressure, you want to hold every variable in your own hands.
有你在，事情就能從想法變成系統。: With you around, ideas become systems.
條理分明、行動有序，能把混亂化為可執行的秩序，成為團隊可依靠的結構者。: Clear and orderly in thought and action. You turn chaos into workable order and become the structure a team can lean on.
控制慾變強、過度理性、失去彈性——系統開始僵化，創造力跟著受限。: The urge to control grows, you get overly rational and lose flexibility. The system stiffens, and creativity shrinks with it.
從「控制」轉為「承載」：讓結構服務目標，而不是讓人服務結構。: Move from controlling to holding: let structure serve the goal, instead of making people serve the structure.

建立安全感與清楚的邊界，說好規則反而讓彼此更自由。: Create safety and clear boundaries. Agreed rules actually make both people freer.
